title: A simple and versatile method for frequent 24 h blood sample collection in healthy older adults
author: Akintola, Jansen, et al.
materials: No validated guidelines were available for older subjects.

steps.title: Identify and prepare venous access
steps.instruction: Visually locate suitable forearm veins (median cubital and median veins), inspect the antecubital fossa, clean the skin with 2 % chlorhexidine, and insert an appropriate cannula; if cannulation fails, apply pressure to the site.

steps.title: Prime line with heparinized saline
steps.instruction: Prepare a continuous saline infusion containing heparin at 100 IU/mL and connect it to the cannula to keep the IV system patent and reduce clotting or phlebitis.

steps.title: Collect blood samples over 24 h
steps.instruction: Draw blood every 10 minutes for a total period of 24 hours, ensuring that the cumulative volume does not exceed 500 mL or 15 % of the participant’s estimated blood volume.

steps.title: Post‑draw site management
steps.instruction: After each draw, inspect the puncture site; if bleeding occurs, apply gentle pressure until it stops, otherwise place a bandage on the site.
